scope: Local GitHub Star call-to-action for the PhiAgent demo page
summary: The current feature-branch demo now shows a responsive GitHub Star call-to-action with the repository's real Star count and explicit post-click guidance. Local browser acceptance passed, but production publication was not started because the checked-out page differs from the current main-branch page and the worktree contains unrelated changes.
evidence: The JavaScript source passes Node.js syntax validation.

A real browser at 1440x900 displayed the call-to-action fully within the first viewport, resolved the repository URL to https://github.com/YuhuaJiang2002/PhiAgent, and loaded the live GitHub Star count as 8.
Clicking the call-to-action changed the local guidance to 'GitHub 已打开' and explicitly instructed the visitor to click Star on the repository page.
A real browser at 390x844 displayed the full call-to-action without clipping, and the browser console contained no warnings or errors.
git diff --check passed for demo/index.html, demo/styles.css, and demo/app.js.
lessons: A static GitHub Pages site should use GitHub's repository Star as the durable like signal instead of presenting a local-only click as a completed vote.
The call-to-action should explain both steps before navigation and retain explicit guidance after the repository opens.
limitations: The production main branch currently serves a different inline-styled demo/index.html than the checked-out feature branch, so this local acceptance does not prove the live URL has changed.
The unauthenticated GitHub repository API can be rate-limited; the repository link remains usable and falls back to a GitHub label when the count cannot load.
next_actions: Choose whether to patch only the currently deployed main-branch page or publish the newer feature-branch page, then deploy and verify the production URL.
